problemStatement.formal: For N : PolygonalNoodle n, N.expectedCrossings d = 2 * N.totalLength / (π * d); and for smooth C¹ curves, smoothExpectedCrossings γ a b d = 2 * planarCurveArcLength γ a b / (π * d) (axiom)
problemStatement.plain: Buffon's Noodle: the expected number of crossings of any curve (polygonal or smooth) of length L with a parallel line grid (spacing d) equals 2L/(πd), depending only on total arc length, not shape.
whyMatters: Fundamental result in geometric probability and integral geometry
Shows that arc length is the invariant that determines intersection count
Special case of the Cauchy-Crofton formula, a cornerstone of integral geometry
Motivates stereological estimation of curve lengths from cross-section counts

proven: Buffon's Noodle for polygons: E[crossings] = 2L/(πd) (proved via linearity of expectation)
Shape independence: same total length → same expected crossings (proved)
needle_equals_noodle: straight needle = any equal-length polygon (proved)
Approximation limit: if polygonal lengths → L, expected crossings → 2L/(πd) (proved)
smooth_shape_independence: smooth curves with same arc length have same expected crossings (proved from axiom)
circle: E[crossings] = 4r/d for circle of radius r (proved)
square: E[crossings] = 8s/(πd) for square of side s (proved)
open: Full formal proof of smooth curve Buffon theorem without axioms (requires kinematic measure theory on line space)
Formal Cauchy-Crofton formula: ∫₀^π ∫₋∞^∞ n(C,(θ,ρ)) dρ dθ = 2·length(C)
Higher-dimensional versions: curves in ℝⁿ crossing hyperplanes
knownResults.goal: Prove E[crossings] = 2L/(πd) for smooth rectifiable curves without axioms, using Mathlib arc length theory and Cauchy-Crofton formula.

currentState.focus: Added approximation limit theorem, Lipschitz bound, arc length definition, proper smooth curve axiom with shape independence. Polygonal case is fully proved; smooth case properly axiomatized.
